approved_descriptions.description: A small, stubby olive-green fish with a cream belly, amber fins, and one dark stripe along its side. A modest little river catch.
A plump copper-orange fish with broad scales, short whiskers, and a thick fan-shaped tail. Rounded features give it a slightly grumpy expression.
A long, narrow fish with a pointed snout, mottled brown-and-moss scales, and a ragged dorsal fin resembling a fern frond.
A sleek crimson fish with cream chevrons along its sides, a sharp triangular dorsal fin, and a deeply forked tail. It should look fast and athletic.
A slender pearl-gray fish with lavender shading and oversized, translucent blue fins that trail like delicate silk. Its flowing silhouette is its defining feature.
A compact turquoise fish with a pale mint belly, rounded fins, and three softly luminous markings along its side. Bright, jewel-like eyes complete its appearance.
A deep violet fish with a dark back, broad angular fins, and small amber markings. Its swept fins create a silhouette reminiscent of bat wings.
A silver-blue fish with an elegantly arched back, a crescent-shaped tail, and one oversized moon-white dorsal fin. Smooth, pale scales give it an otherworldly sheen.
A regal emerald fish with large jade scales edged in gold, a crown-shaped dorsal crest, and a broad, layered tail. It should resemble a living treasure.
A large, nearly circular fish with brilliant golden scales, an ivory belly, and orange-red fins spreading outward like a sunburst. Its bold shape should immediately distinguish it from Marlo.
